Trump Makes Third Texas Trip in a Month as Paxton Faces Tight Senate Race

7 Oct at 1:51 pm
View Comments
Post Views: 67
Newslooks Morning Edition J.Mansour
10243 posts
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:51
Instaread

Trump Makes Third Texas Trip in a Month as Paxton Faces Tight Senate Race/ Newslooks/ WASHINGTON/ J. Mansour/ President Donald Trump returns to Texas Wednesday for his third visit in a month as Republicans defend unexpectedly competitive Senate and House races. Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton faces Democrat James Talarico, who leads in recent polling despite Trump’s comfortable statewide victory in 2024. The San Antonio rally comes amid voter concerns about high costs, the Iran war and an uneasy political alliance between Trump and Paxton.

Quick Look

  • Third Texas visit: Trump is scheduled to rally in San Antonio alongside Paxton.
  • Senate contest: An Oct. 3 Siena College poll showed Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 45% among likely voters.
  • National headwinds: A Reuters/Ipsos poll put Trump’s approval at 32%, with Democrats leading Republicans among registered voters.
  • Congressional stakes: A Texas Senate loss would complicate Republicans’ effort to retain their slim majority.
  • House races: Republicans are also defending competitive seats in South Texas.
  • Uneasy alliance: Trump has criticized Paxton publicly while emphasizing the importance of electing him.

Deep Look

Trump Returns to Texas to Support Ken Paxton

President Donald Trump heads to Texas Wednesday for his third trip to the state in a month, underscoring the unexpectedly difficult election landscape facing Republicans in a longtime stronghold.

Trump is scheduled to speak in San Antonio with Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton, who is competing against Democrat James Talarico in the Nov. 3 election.

A Republican defeat would threaten the party’s effort to preserve its slim Senate majority and represent a significant setback in a state Trump won by 14 percentage points in 2024.

The visit follows a Trump-centered midterm convention in Dallas organized partly to help Paxton mobilize Republican voters.

Although Trump has repeatedly campaigned for his longtime ally, he has also criticized him. Last week, he called Paxton “a pain in the ass sometimes” before saying Republicans “need Ken so badly.”

Republican-Leaning States Become Midterm Battlegrounds

Trump’s repeated Texas visits are part of a broader campaign push through states Republicans had expected to hold comfortably.

His 32-day campaign blitz has included Texas, Oklahoma, Alabama, Ohio and Nebraska. Vice President JD Vance has also campaigned in Alaska.

Trump and Vance carried all six states in the 2024 presidential election. Republicans now face competitive contests across territory that previously appeared secure.

Voter frustration over high costs and the war with Iran has contributed to Trump’s record-low approval ratings.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll completed Monday found his approval at 32%. Among registered voters, Democrats led Republicans 44% to 37%.

Talarico’s Polling Lead Raises Stakes for Trump

Trump surprised some Republicans in May when he endorsed Paxton over longtime Sen. John Cornyn in the party runoff. Republican leaders had viewed Cornyn as the safer general election candidate.

The party is now spending heavily to defend seats it once expected to win without difficulty.

Recent Texas polling has shown Talarico ahead. A Siena College survey released Oct. 3 put the Democrat at 51% and Paxton at 45% among likely voters.

James Henson, director of the Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin, said a Senate defeat would be “devastating for Republicans and devastating for Donald Trump” because of the president’s support for Paxton.

“I think the president clearly will do a lot to try to avoid that outcome,” Henson said.

Competitive Texas House Races Add to Republican Concerns

The Republican challenge extends beyond the Senate race, with competitive House seats in South Texas also drawing attention and spending.

Trump’s political operation has invested millions in contested congressional races.

In San Antonio, Republican Carlos De La Cruz, an Air Force veteran, is running in a newly redrawn district created through Republican-led remapping. Democrats have criticized the changes as a partisan gerrymander.

De La Cruz is expected to speak at Wednesday’s rally, bringing another congressional contest into Trump’s effort to energize Texas supporters.

Trump and Paxton Navigate an Uneasy Alliance

Despite their shared political interests, Trump and Paxton’s relationship has shown signs of strain.

Trump has publicly mocked Paxton’s clothing, speaking style and appearance. Meanwhile, The New York Times reported that Paxton told donors Republican candidates’ polling numbers declined after the Dallas convention centered on Trump.

“So to be honest with you, the numbers, when we did that convention, it dropped our numbers. Everybody’s numbers dropped,” Paxton said in a recording.

His campaign has disputed suggestions that the comments constituted criticism of Trump. A spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.

Brandon Rottinghaus, a political science professor at the University of Houston, said mobilizing Trump’s supporters was “necessary but not sufficient” for Paxton.

The San Antonio rally will put that strategy on display as Republicans try to turn strong support for Trump among their base into enough votes to protect a Senate seat and retain control of Congress.
